title: John Sangster's late-blooming cornet
summary: A rough cornettist Polites played with before Johnson's band, who suddenly played brilliantly at the 1948 convention, joined Graham Bell as drummer, and killed his mother.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And what about John's sewing stuff?

He was the chap I used to play with most of all before I joined the Johnson band. Mm-hmm. He is a very keen cornet player. But, he was rough. He was pretty awful for a while. I can remember playing with him and thinking, oh, gosh, this is no value at all. He's so far off. He's sort of very keen, but he just can't get it. Suddenly, it all came. Obviously, he'd been practicing and thinking about it, but these things take time. Suddenly, it all sort of came to his fingertips and the 1948 Jazz Convention, he suddenly surprised everyone by playing a wonderful driving sort of cornet. No particular style. Mm-hmm. It was just tremendous stuff. He didn't keep it up for long and then he joined the Graham Bell Band as drummer on their second tour. Mm-hmm. He got into modern playing then and he's been on that since. Modern drummer now? Yes, and cornet. Mm-hmm. He was the one who killed his mother with an axe because she wouldn't let him go to a Graham Bell concert, which made things quite worrying sometimes. I can't believe that. Are you making that up? No, this sounds like an early New Orleans legend, I know. No, he did this, but he was so young they sort of let him off. And let him off. Sometimes I used to think I'd better not make any mistakes when playing with him. Yeah. But there was no sign of that in him really, except that he was terribly enthusiastic.
